Throughout this series, we’ll investigate pivotal topics and their multifaceted impacts on our democratic society. We’ll explore the effects of AI and social media on democracy, as well as the interesting dynamics of how technology affects democracy. 
In each episode, we'll be joined by an array of policymakers, experts, and ordinary people, each offering rich insights and diverse perspectives on the ethical, regulatory, and societal ramifications of technology, AI and social media. Our discussions will tackle controversial and complex topics, from potential biases in AI and the need for content regulation to the ethical dilemmas arising from advancements in artificial intelligence.
As we uncover the impacts of AI and social media on our societal norms, individual rights, and the very fabric of democracy, we hope to enlighten you with insightful and interesting perspectives on the many new ways to participate in the democratic process.

Audiobooks are the modern bridge between the ancient art of storytelling and the fast-paced rhythm of contemporary life. They transform the written word into a living, breathing experience through the power of voice. Whether narrated by the author or a skilled performer, audiobooks carry the emotion, tone, and rhythm that can often be lost on the printed page.
They invite listeners into worlds of imagination, knowledge, and emotion—through headphones, speakers, or car stereos—turning any moment into an opportunity to learn, feel, or escape. In essence, audiobooks are literature in motion. They allow stories to accompany us as we walk, drive, or rest. They are for the commuter seeking inspiration, the traveler longing for company, or the lifelong learner expanding their mind without the constraint of a page.
The beauty of an audiobook lies not only in its content but in the intimacy of its delivery. The human voice adds warmth, depth, and subtlety—transforming reading into listening, and listening into an immersive, personal journey. In a world where time feels scarce, audiobooks offer a way to reclaim it. They make knowledge and art more accessible, inclusive, and dynamic. They remind us that storytelling began with the voice—and through audiobooks, the voice continues to shape how we connect with stories today.

title: The Grace Fueled Wife
author: Beatriz Vargas
description:
Are you sitting in a marriage that feels empty? 
Struggling to connect with your husband or wondering why communication in your marriage feels so hard? 
Maybe you feel lonely in your marriage even though you’re still living under the same roof.
Maybe you’re telling yourself you’re just sticking it out for the kids… and what really keeps you in the marriage is your commitment to God.
If this is you, I’ve been there. And I want to help you reconnect in your marriage, rebuild emotional intimacy, and feel cherished again.
Hey, I’m Beatriz Vargas — a Christian marriage coach, Jesus-loving wife, and mom. I’ve been married for over 15 years, but for the first five years of our marriage we struggled with constant conflict, poor communication, and emotional disconnection.
I was busy telling my husband all the things he was doing wrong — what he needed to change, how he needed Jesus, and what he needed to do to make me happy.
We tried marriage counseling, small groups, and all the things we were told would fix our marriage. 
Nothing worked… and eventually we separated.
But learning how communication, emotional safety, and grace actually work inside a marriage changed everything.
Today, my husband and I have the affectionate, emotionally connected marriage I once thought was impossible.
On The Grace Fueled Wife Podcast, you’ll learn how to:
• communicate more effectively with your husband
 • break unhealthy conflict cycles in marriage
 • rebuild emotional intimacy and connection
 • stop feeling lonely in your marriage
 • navigate difficult conversations with grace
 • strengthen your Christian marriage even when your husband isn’t changing
If you feel like you’re the only one trying to save your marriage… if you’re tired of having the same arguments over and over… or if you’re longing to feel close again, this podcast will help you understand what’s really happening beneath the surface.
Each week we talk about communication in marriage, conflict resolution, emotional intimacy, and how faith and grace can help restore connection in even the most difficult seasons of marriage.
So grab your journal, take a deep breath, and let’s start creating the connected, grace-fueled marriage you’ve been praying for.
Connect: Beatriz@thegracefueledwife.com

title: Serious Money Podcast
author: Gareth Shears
description:
There are loads of money podcasts. None of them are really built for people who've already got money.

Most money content is aimed at people just getting started. Budgeting, saving, the basics. Serious Money is for everyone who's moved well past that. Business owners. Higher earners. People approaching retirement. People with real complexity and real decisions to make, who are tired of content that's either so jargon-heavy it sends you to sleep, or a sales pitch dressed up as advice.

Hosted by Gareth, who has spent over 18 years in financial planning, and Chris, who has spent the last ten years working in financial services with clients making exactly these decisions, and who at 35 is living most of them himself. Both from Newport in Wales, which means you're getting two people who've never been particularly impressed by the London financial bubble.

Every episode goes into one topic properly. No surface-level stuff. Then real questions from real listeners, and occasionally a guest who can add something we can't.

What makes it different: we disagree, genuinely and not for effect. We tell you what we'd actually do with our own money. And we say the things most people in this industry won't say in public. Not to be controversial, but because you deserve a straight answer.

Got a question you want answered on the show? Send us a voice note or message on Instagram, @seriousmoneypod. The best ones go straight into the Q&A.

The content of this podcast is for general information and entertainment only. It is not personal financial advice and should not be relied on as such. Neither host is providing regulated financial advice through this podcast. Always seek advice from a qualified, regulated professional before making financial decisions. Capital is at risk and past performance is not a guide to future returns.

title: TECHNICALLY JOYFUL - Building Change Capacity in the Age of AI
author: Gabrielle Kohlmeier - AI Leadership & Change Capacity
description:
Change is coming faster than ever. Joy helps us keep up — and shape what comes next.


Look closely at the people doing hard things extraordinarily well — creating change that lasts, building what didn’t exist before, turning ambitious ideas into reality — and you’ll notice something: joy is often part of the fuel.


They are technically joyful.


Host Gabrielle Kohlmeier has used joy again and again to build with others what seemed impossible — and create outcomes beyond what anyone thought possible. In Technically Joyful, she shares what she’s learned and brings together people doing hard, consequential things differently: leaders, builders, thinkers, and wonderfully curious humans exploring what they’re seeing, what they’re learning, what isn’t obvious yet, and what the rest of us can use.


We’ll tackle the hard questions. We’ll make the invisible work of change visible. We’ll find signal in the noise. And we’ll get practical about what actually helps people and organizations move — from technology, strategy, and systems to judgment, incentives, relationships, courage, and the wonderfully human messiness in between.


Instead of fear as fuel, we use curiosity, connection, usefulness, awe, and the gentle persistence of joy. Joy gives us energy to engage with hard things — to stay curious longer, see more possibilities, connect more dots, and keep going.

Every episode is designed to leave you seeing something differently, understanding something useful, and feeling more capable of acting — at work, in your organization, and in the much bigger experiment we’re all part of as AI reshapes our world.


Expect hard questions, fascinating people, useful ideas, unexpected connections — and to come out stronger than you went in.


Change is a muscle. Joy helps us build it.


Welcome to Technically Joyful.



Some Questions We‘ll Explore: 

  • Why does being a beginner feel so threatening once you’re successful?
  • What happens when the work that disappears was also the training ground?
  • Why do some people seem energized by uncertainty while others freeze?
  • What are we losing when efficiency becomes the dominant measure of value?
  • How do you know when doing nothing is actually the riskier choice?
  • What becomes possible when we stop treating curiosity as frivolous?
  • What does AI reveal about work that was already broken?
  • How do we keep our judgment while changing how we use it?
  • What becomes more valuable — not less — as AI gets better?
  • Why might joy actually make us better at doing hard things?

Brain Health FM is for high achievers who want their energy, focus and clarity back, without the hype. If you've built a demanding career on sharp thinking and lately it costs more to produce, this show is for you.


Dr Sui Wong is a consultant neurologist and neuro-ophthalmologist who has spent more than 25 years helping tens of thousands of patients. description:
Hi! Welcome to The Case for Classics ! I'm your host, Maira Zaidi.


I created this podcast to inspire a new generation of learners to discover the enduring value of Classical Studies. Through conversations with leading scholars, educators, students, and professionals, I explore how the ancient world is not a relic of the past but a living legacy that continues to shape our language, literature, philosophy, politics, and culture.


At its heart, the podcast seeks to make Classics more accessible and inclusive by introducing Latin, Greek, and Ancient History to students from all backgrounds, especially those who may never have encountered them before. By sharing insights from people across the field, I hope to demonstrate how the study of antiquity remains relevant to the questions and challenges we face today.


My goal is to make the case that an education in Classics develops intellectual curiosity, analytical thinking, cultural understanding, and clear communication—qualities that prepare students not only to succeed in careers such as academia, law, medicine, public service, journalism, business, and science, but also to become thoughtful, engaged citizens capable of understanding the complexities of the modern world.


Through this podcast, I hope to inspire young people to discover the ancient world as part of our shared global heritage and recognize that Classics remains one of the most relevant and rewarding fields of study today.


Thank you so much for listening. Whether you're a lifelong Classicist or you're just discovering the ancient world for the very first time, I'm so glad you're here. Let's make the case for Classics together!


Maira Zaidi

Founder, Acta Diurna Classics – An Archive of Classical Inquiry

title: What’s Flowing? A walking podcast with Flavia Marfella
author: Flavia Marfella
description:
What’s Flowing?

Conversations while everything changes.

What’s Flowing? is a walking podcast from Malmö, Sweden and part of the Everyday Flow ecosystem.


Each episode is recorded while walking. Sometimes it’s quiet. Most of the time it’s windy. Sometimes you can hear the city, the sea, a dog, footsteps, or life happening around us. That’s part of it.

Think of it as dropping into a phone call between two people who happen to be out for a walk,  talking, noticing, thinking out loud, following an idea and seeing where it goes.

Because walking does something to a conversation. When the body moves, ideas seem to move too. Thoughts connect differently. There’s less pressure to perform and more room for curiosity.


We might talk about creativity, work, identity, technology, midlife, starting again, living abroad, relationships, wellbeing, or something completely unexpected. The point isn’t to tell you what to change next. It’s to stay curious about what’s already moving.


About the host

Flavia Marfella, is an expat based in Malmö, Italian, who has spent years working with innovation, ideas and change. She’s a certified coach and positive psychology practitioner and app developer, curious by nature and always interested in what helps people, ideas and possibilities move forward.


Everyday Flow is an evolving world of ideas, projects and experiences built around living with more curiosity, intention and flow. What’s Flowing? is its conversational side — a place to meet people, follow interesting threads and keep each other company while everything keeps changing.

No perfect studio. No formulas. No pressure to reinvent yourself.

Just put on your headphones and walk with us.

Let’s see what’s flowing.

title: A journey through feminist agroecology
author: CIDSE & AgroecologyNow-CAWR
description:
Why is agroecology not possible without feminism? What does feminism have to do with the food you eat? Agroecology is gaining steam as the way forward to sustainable, just and healthy food systems, however, there is still ample confusion about why the feminist perspective is important, how it aligns with agroecology and what it has to offer to food system transformation. It is often confused with gender equity, whereas feminist values include but go far beyond gender. 


In this podcast activists, researchers and practitioners who dedicate their lives to feminism and agroecology share how women (and others) are invisibly sustaining the food system, what it means to place ‘life’, rather than profit, in the centre of the food system, and what food systems would look like if they were based on feminist values. We explore how the oppression of women forms part of systemic oppression against anyone who falls out of the white, heterosexual, cis-male box, what decolonial and indigenous feminisms offer to the agroecology movement, and how to strengthen that movement from a feminist perspective. 


This podcast is a collaboration between The Centre for Agroecology, Water and Resilience (CAWR) and CIDSE.


This project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under the Marie Sklodowska-Curie grant agreement No 844637.

Here, we explore how to listen—to the body, to each other, to the wisdom found in life's challenges, and to the imaginal blueprint revealed through our Human Design. We talk about releasing old stories, trusting ourselves in our messy evolution, and softening into deeper truth instead of pushing harder.
This podcast sits at the intersection of personal transformation and collective reimagining. It's about pausing in those disorienting moments when structures are crumbling, choosing curiosity over control, and accessing our full creative potential to build something genuinely new.
This is not a podcast with all the answers—it's a love letter to the world and a space to witness authentic stories that hope to affirm and awaken something within you.

It's the kind of stuff that's too specific and too strange to explain away, like a shadow that keeps showing up... A sound that comes from the wrong room... A child who's made friends with something you can't see. I tell these stories honestly, unhurried, and with full respect for how terrifying they actually are.


What makes this show different? It's drag, honey! I bring the warmth, wit, and the occasional dramatic pause that turns an already-creepy story into something you feel in your chest. I'm not here to shock you. I'm here to sit with you in the dark for a little while.


No gimmicks. No dramatic sound design pretending to do the work (well, maybe some creepy music boxes). But really, it's just me, the stories, and you.


If you love paranormal podcasts, ghost stories, or anything that makes you double-check the hallway before bed, you're home! Follow Pink Hair Ain't Scared wherever you listen. Tell a friend. And maybe, just maybe, leave a light on.
